t56.subject: [investigation] f_ackermann residual gotos — VERIFIED genuinely irreducible (no CFG bug)
t56.description:
RESOLVED via ground-truth tracing (commit fccaf7e60). Investigated whether f_ackermann's 16 residual gotos stem from a fixable CFG-construction bug. They do NOT. Two of my earlier hypotheses were WRONG and are now disproven by instrumentation:

1. WRONG (and fabricated-as-done earlier): "merge_linear_blocks won't merge call-terminated blocks." That edit never even applied (targeted wrong file). Calls are not the fragmentation driver.
2. WRONG: "7 unresolved CBRANCH targets / dropped edges." Added UNLACE_CFG_BUILD_TRACE to build_function_from_insns: f_ackermann builds 90 blocks / 90 leaders / ZERO dropped edges. The "c0x19f8"-style values in IR text are just the Const target operand every CBRANCH carries (normal pcode) — not missing edges.

VERIFIED ACTUAL CAUSE: f_ackermann's compiled CFG is genuinely irreducible. UNLACE_SPLIT_TRACE shows split_irreducible_entries detects ONE SCC of 68 body blocks with 22 distinct entry blocks (e.g. BB_36->BB_33, BB_47->BB_29, BB_50->BB_25 — branches into the middle of sibling chains). Tarjan SCC + >1-entry detection (irreducible.rs) is textbook-correct. node_split is correctly STUCK (every single-entry split is non-shrinking, largest_body stays 68, split_now=0 round 0 — raising MAX_SPLIT_ROUNDS cannot help). The double recursion was lowered by the compiler to a multi-entry state machine; the 16 gotos are HONEST output. The golden's goto-free form is IDA reconstructing semantics, not preserving this CFG.

DELIVERABLE: two reusable env-gated traces (UNLACE_CFG_BUILD_TRACE, UNLACE_SPLIT_TRACE), byte-identical-safe. The only path to fewer gotos here is DREAM multi-header/abnormal-entry structuring (separate active frontier, commits ...01d204384 nested-cyclic-decomposition), NOT a lifter/CFG fix. No code fix warranted; closing.

t60.subject: Fix phantom argument over-detection inflating precision denominator
t60.description:
Fixed phantom argument over-detection in var_naming.rs. Root cause: `classify_variables` assigned `VarRole::Argument` to every arg-register read in the entry block (lines 270-277, 299-305, 350-353), regardless of whether the register index exceeded `inferred_params.len()`. At `-O2`, registers like rdx (arg_idx=2) and rcx (arg_idx=3) were used as compiler-generated loop counters but got promoted to phantom `a3`/`a4` arguments. 

Solution: Added param_count guard at all three assignment sites (entry-block Copy, entry-block direct-read, whole-function live-in fallback) — only assign `VarRole::Argument` when `arg_idx < inferred_params.len()`. Added `UNLACE_VAR_NAMING_TRACE` env flag with per-decision trace lines (shows phantom arg rejections with reason).

Results: 
- leaked_temp_decls: 324 → 311 (−13)
- precision: 37.5% → 37.9%
- phantom aX count: 20+ → 14 (remaining 14 are genuine — varargs, tail-call chains)
- All gates green: passes 1157/1157, semantic-report 25/0, quality_smoke 7/7, clippy/fmt clean
- arm64_features budget updated (3→4) due to one rdx loop counter now named c1 instead of suppressed a3

Verification: UNLACE_TYPE_TRACE=1 cargo xtask type-recovery-report shows 14 remaining phantom aX decls (down from 20+); sum_for/sum_do/sum_while now have no a3/a4 declarations.
